query: adjacent subtopics, prerequisites, and applications of The dot-com bubble

results.title: What actually popped the bubble in March 2000
results.content: The mechanism and trigger that popped the bubble in March 2000 is the natural next question once a lesson establishes that it burst. Rate rises, lock-up expiries, and a shift in profit expectations are well documented.

results.title: Speculative bubbles before the internet
results.content: Earlier speculative bubbles, including tulip mania and the South Sea episode, place the internet boom in a reusable historical pattern rather than as a one-off piece of tech history.

results.title: Which dot-com era companies survived
results.content: An applied follow-up is which era companies survived and what they did differently. Amazon and others turned the repricing into a stronger business rather than disappearing with the speculation.

results.title: Prerequisites: reading a stock index
results.content: A prerequisite for going deeper is knowing how the NASDAQ Composite differs from the NASDAQ-100 so peak and trough figures are not swapped.
